embeds.description:
Rapid7 researchers discovered a critical argument injection vulnerability in the open-source Gogs Git service that allows authenticated users to remotely execute code on a Gogs server via malicious branch names during merge operations. The vulnerability has remained unpatched for over two months after Rapid7 reported it to the Gogs maintainer, who did not respond to status update requests or disclosure deferral offers. Rapid7 published analysis of the vulnerability on the day of this article's publication. The vulnerability could lead to Gogs server compromise, cross-tenant data breaches, credential theft, lateral movement, and software supply chain attacks.
